chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Abdullah ibn al-Rahman al-Asam, from Abdullah al-Batl, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) went out one day while holding the hand of Ali (peace be upon him) and said: 'O people of the Ansar, O people of Banu Hashim, O people of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, I am Muhammad, I am the Messenger of God. Indeed, I was created from a merciful clay, along with four from my Ahl al-Bayt: I, Ali, Hamza, and Ja'far.' A speaker said: 'O Messenger of God, will these four be with you as riders on the Day of Resurrection?'

He said: 'May your mother be bereaved of you! Indeed, no one but these four will ride on that day: I, Ali, Fatimah, and Salih, the Prophet of God. As for me, I will be on the Buraq. As for my daughter Fatimah, she will be on my camel al-Kaswa. As for Salih, he will be on the Camel of God which was immolated. As for Ali, he will be on a camel from the camels of Paradise, its rein made of pearl, adorned with two green harnesses.'

He will stand between Paradise and Hell. On that day, the people will be overwhelmed with sweat, so a wind will blow from the direction of the Throne, drying their sweat. The angels, prophets, and the truthful will say: 'This is none but a nearby angel or a dispatched prophet.' Then a caller will announce: 'This is not a nearby angel nor a dispatched prophet, but Ali ibn Abi Talib, the brother of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) in this world and the Hereafter.'

key_terms.أَخُوهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Brother of the Messenger of God
key_terms.نَاقَةِ اللَّهِ: Camel of God (referring to Prophet Salih)

ai.seo_question: Who are the four riders on the Day of Resurrection according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal underscores the unique eschatological status of the Ahl al-Bayt, specifically highlighting Ali ibn Abi Talib's singular honor of riding a celestial camel with a yaqut bridle, distinct from the mounts of other prophets. It reinforces the Shia doctrine of the Prophet's familial lineage as the exclusive recipients of divine intercession and recognition on the Day of Judgment, where Ali is identified not merely as a companion but as the 'brother' of the Prophet in both the temporal and eternal realms.
